about: What real use, and the person Pit Board is for, showed must change or must stay true in Windstorm Pit Board, and the version each is due in. A lesson here is a gate, not a note: tests/test_g21_promises.py (G21.14) refuses a version while a row due in it is not built, and refuses the version after it until the row says where it was proven on a real machine.
how_to_use: A new lesson gets a row the day it is learned: what was seen, the promise, a codon in DNA-STRAND-MASTER-PLAN.md, the version it is due in, and a tracking issue when work is left.
When it is built: put the name of its test in 'test'. The test must exist under tests/ and be named with the row's codon (test_G10_5_... for G10.5).
When it has been seen to work on a real machine: say which machine, which version and when in 'proven'.

'ship_in' moves only with a reason in 'moved_why'. A row whose owner is 'person' was seen by the person Pit Board is for, on their own machine: its date moves only by their word, restated in 'moved_by_person'.
A row is never deleted. A promise that turns out wrong is closed by a row that says why.
A lesson that was heard and not taken goes under 'declined' with the reason, so that nothing is dropped without a word.

rows.seen: 2026-11-22, the overnight stress test, an Intel Mac: one test folder had the 0.1.1 candidate installed from its commit with setup --folder and its own Pit Board home, while other test folders on the machine had 0.1.0. The plugin's own bin/pitboard in that folder ran 0.1.1, but the home's stable launcher, which the status line wrapper calls, ran 0.1.0: no version is in update/good-versions before the self-check of G21.3 exists, so G21.4 step 6 took the first entry in installed_plugins.json, whatever its version. No effect in 0.1.1, whose status line and hook code are those of 0.1.0. The fix (G21.4 step 6, plan 1.15) was seen on a real Intel Mac test account on 2026-11-22 at 15:37Z, Claude Code 2.1.330: two folders, each with its own local-scope catalog, the 0.1.0 release installed first and the fixed code (0.1.1) second, and a Pit Board home with no self-check yet. The 0.1.1 release's stable launcher ran 0.1.0 ("0.1.0 (installed 0.1.1, hooks gen 1)"), and the fixed one ran 0.1.1. Still to see before 0.1.2's tag: a home set up by 0.1.0 or 0.1.1 whose stable copy the first session start of a folder on 0.1.2 refreshes (plan 1.16), so its status line runs the new launcher; and a restore of ten or more sessions of one home on a real machine that leaves one whole copy.
rows.promise: Before any version has passed a self-check, the stable launcher runs the highest installed version, not the first one listed, so the status line never runs code older than the newest install.
rows.proven: 2026-11-22 on an Intel Mac test machine, Claude Code 2.1.330, the 0.1.2 candidate (main at edda023b, the refresh code, with version 0.1.2) installed in every test folder from a git source, three sightings, each for what it is. (1) The refresh of an old home by the real upgrade path: a Pit Board home set up by 0.1.1's own `setup --folder`, whose copy answered '0.1.0 (installed 0.1.2, hooks gen 1)', got its first session start on 0.1.2 at a clean reboot's restore (18:05:07Z); its log then said 'stable launcher before-0.1.2 -> 0.1.2, backup kept', and its copy answered '0.1.2 (installed 0.1.2, hooks gen 1)', with `.prev` equal to 0.1.1's launcher, no leftovers, and the status line wrapper running through it. (2) A ten-session restore of one home on the same reboot, NOT simultaneous: the restore tool started the ten sessions about 5 s apart (18:05:12Z to 18:05:56Z, load about 86 at the end of the restore), the first hook refreshed the copy in 1.4 s and the other nine found it current; one whole copy was left, checked as in (1). (3) Ten real session-start hooks of one home at the same moment, at 19:21:46Z under load 39.8, 67.2 and 78.9 (1, 5 and 15 minutes): a home set up by 0.1.1's own setup code, ten hooks from the candidate's installed version folder in the plugin cache, released within 0.3 ms; up to 10 refresh folders existed at once and all ten exited 0 with their SessionStart output. Six refreshed the copy; four stopped at the 3 s check under the load and wrote nothing. At the end: one whole copy (the candidate's files, copied-from 0.1.2), `.prev` equal to 0.1.1's, no leftovers, and the copy answered '0.1.2 (installed 0.1.2, hooks gen 1)'. The same race runs in CI on Linux and macOS (tests/test_g21_stablecopy.py, twelve hooks).

rows.seen: 2026-11-22, round 6 of the overnight stress test, a clean reboot of an Intel Mac in the middle of the work: in a fresh macOS test account, setup --folder --apply and --undo ran in a loop. 7 of 28 installs failed in claude plugin install while it cloned the plugin (once before the reboot, 6 times as the network went down). Each failed apply undid itself and left the folder clean (G18.1 step 6), but the message kept only the last line of Claude Code's error: 'claude plugin install failed: and the repository exists.; undone'. Later the same day, the skill's owner's install from the catalog in a clean test account (Claude Code 2.1.280, no GitHub key) failed with 'Host key verification failed' and 'Permission denied (publickey)': the clone went over SSH. A fresh macOS test account with no GitHub key (Claude Code 2.1.330) had installed over HTTPS 21 times; its one passing failure said 'HTTPS clone failed, retrying with SSH'. The real output of both failed clones, recorded with no terminal as setup runs it, is kept in tests/fixtures/claude_plugin_errors and replayed by the row's test.
rows.promise: When a claude plugin command fails, setup --folder shows Claude Code's error from its first error line to its end, not only its last line. When that error shows the clone failed over SSH because GitHub accepted no key ('Host key verification failed' or 'Permission denied (publickey)'), it says so first, in plain words: Claude Code could not clone the plugin from GitHub over SSH; this account is not set up for GitHub over SSH (GitHub accepted no key from it). Then what to do: check that this machine reaches github.com over HTTPS, or add a GitHub key to this account, and run the same setup --folder again.
rows.proven: 2026-11-22T14:37Z, the code of commit 527ba6c run for real in two test accounts with no GitHub key, each in a scratch folder whose own catalog held a github entry it could not clone: setup --folder --apply exited 6, put the folder back, and showed the plain-words lines first, then Claude Code's whole error, every line within 100 columns and none cut. Claude Code 2.1.280 on Linux (the real Pit Board entry, cloned over SSH only): the SSH form. Claude Code 2.1.330 on an Intel Mac (an entry for a repository that does not exist, so HTTPS failed first): the HTTPS-then-SSH form, with Claude Code's own advice line, and its progress lines left out.

The status line went silent while its setting stayed, and a hook from a session still running ran the orphaned folder's code in full.
rows.promise: `pitboard uninstall` takes Pit Board and everything it made off the computer, however it was set up: plan first, `--apply` does it, three answers for every read, the status line setting back to exactly the person's value (absent if they had none) and nothing else in a settings file changed by Pit Board, byte for byte where nothing else wrote the file, or (unreadable) never touched. What is the person's (the asks, the log, the setup record, setup's backups) is kept and counted; `--delete-asks-and-log` deletes it only at a terminal, by typing the count. A census is the last thing printed, and a second run is safe. All of it is one file, `pitboard/leave.py`, which the stable copy carries and runs alone with no plugin folder anywhere. After Claude Code's own uninstall, no orphaned code runs, the status line names `~/.pitboard/bin/pitboard uninstall`, and a live hook logs one line saying Pit Board was removed. Proven on a stock Linux VM, then in a clean Mac test account, then one real Claude Code session's status line seen to come back as it was (or written as not seen); the README's by-hand lines for a copy from before 0.1.3 run once as written on a stock VM.
rows.proven: Seen 2026-11-23 on the merged code (main bab844dd) in a stock Ubuntu 24.04.5 virtual machine (its own python3 3.12.3), with Claude Code 2.1.330 and 2.1.280 and no sign-in, a fresh user for each case, Pit Board 0.1.2 installed from the catalog as the README says and the merged code laid over its folder; the base image was unchanged afterwards. (A, 2.1.330) After Claude Code's own `plugin uninstall` (the registry row emptied, the folder marked `.orphaned_at`): the status line said `Pit Board was removed by Claude Code · run ~/.pitboard/bin/pitboard uninstall` beside the person's own; a hook from the marked folder printed nothing and wrote one log line saying so; the session start had brought `leave.py` into the 0.1.2 home. That command, run as printed, took Pit Board's entry out of the settings file Claude Code had rewritten and put the person's status line back (the census said just that, not byte for byte), kept and counted the ask, and a second run said nothing of Pit Board was there; the kept line's `rm -r ~/.pitboard`, run as printed, removed the rest. (B, 2.1.280) The plugin's own `uninstall --apply` with a folder install, a user install and a project install: the folder's `settings.local.json` was as before, byte for byte; the user settings file ended with the person's own status line back and the rest as Claude Code's own uninstall left it; the census said Pit Board had put the file back byte for byte before that uninstall changed its entries, which the run did not check between the two steps; the project install was kept and named, and its printed line, run as printed, took it off. (C, 2.1.330) On a 0.1.2 home after Claude Code's own uninstall, the README's two by-hand lines, run as written, put the person's status line back and left only `lanes/`, `lanes.json` and `logs/`. (D, 2.1.330) The delete asked without a terminal was refused and changed nothing; at a terminal a wrong count changed nothing, and the right count took Pit Board, the asks and the log off. (E, 2.1.280, no `claude` on the PATH) Exit 11; the settings file was byte for byte what setup found; the copy stayed; both printed lines, run as printed, took the installs off, and a second run finished. Seen 2026-11-23 on two Macs, each in a clean test account with no Claude Code and no sign-in, on the python3 that comes with Apple's developer tools (3.9.6, asked from inside the run): an Intel desktop (macOS 13.7.8) on the code before the census's kept lines were joined into one (the only difference: those lines), and an Apple silicon Mac (macOS 27.2.1) on the merged code. Each time: a stand-in put the plugin's files and one registry row where an install would, setup made its 7 changes, and one ask was recorded. After a stand-in for Claude Code's own uninstall (the registry row emptied and the folder marked as seen on Linux with two Claude Code versions), the status line said Pit Board was removed and named the command in the copy that stays; a hook from the marked folder did nothing and wrote one line saying so. The delete asked without a terminal was refused and changed nothing. The copy's own uninstall, run by itself, took Pit Board off, removed the status line setting it had added (the account had none before), kept the asks and the log and counted them (1 ask in 1 lane log), and a second run said nothing of Pit Board was there. The kept line's command, run exactly as printed, removed what was kept, and the account was as found. Not seen: a real Claude Code install and its own uninstall on a Mac; a real signed-in session's status line coming back; a Mac without Apple's developer tools.

rows.promise: The tag's fresh-clone check refuses a tag while a row due in that version has an empty `proven`. A row that can only be proven after its release (a count over days) carries a named exception field with its reason, read by the check; there is no blanket rule that would force a false proven line.
rows.proven: 2026-11-23, on a throwaway tag that existed only in a local clone (its remote removed, never pushed): a fresh clone of main 28a6403e, one local commit setting plugin.json, `__version__` and the CHANGELOG heading to 0.1.3, tagged v0.1.3, then `git clone --branch v0.1.3` of it. In that clone the tag check refused the tag: "P18 is due in 0.1.3 and has no proven line", "P19 is due in 0.1.3 and has no proven line". After a second local commit that filled those two proven lines with throwaway text and the tag moved to it, a fresh clone of the tag passed the check and listed P15 as proven only after the release. Linux, git 2.43.0, Python 3.12.3.
